title: A Reflex Is Not the Hurt

scenes.tts: A paw pulls away from a touch. Does that tell you how much it hurts?
scenes.visual: Title card: A Reflex Is Not the Hurt. A mouse paw lifting from a filament. Question: does that tell you how much it hurts?
scenes.narration: A paw pulls away from a touch. Does that tell you how much it hurts?

scenes.tts: Every behavioural result so far was a withdrawal threshold. A reflex is easy to mistake for pain.
scenes.visual: The withdrawal-threshold plot from earlier, shrunk to a corner, tagged: behavioural readout, a reflex measure. Small tags beside it for the other results: recordings, expression, immune assays.
scenes.narration: Every behavioural result so far was a withdrawal threshold. A reflex is easy to mistake for pain.

scenes.tts: Corder and colleagues imaged neurons in the basolateral amygdala of male mice, across repeated sessions.
scenes.visual: A mouse with a head-mounted miniature microscope. Inset: a field of basolateral amygdala neurons. Label: Corder, Ahanonu and colleagues; male mice.
scenes.narration: Corder and colleagues imaged neurons in the basolateral amygdala of male mice, across repeated sessions.

scenes.tts: One ensemble responded to noxious stimuli and encoded their unpleasantness.
scenes.visual: A noxious stimulus icon; a subset of neurons in the field flashes together. Label: ensemble encoding negative valence.
scenes.narration: One ensemble responded to noxious stimuli and encoded their unpleasantness.

scenes.tts: After a nerve injury, innocuous stimuli recruited the same ensemble.
scenes.visual: A light-touch icon; after an injury marker, the same subset flashes.
scenes.narration: After a nerve injury, innocuous stimuli recruited the same ensemble.

scenes.tts: Then they tagged those neurons genetically, and silenced them.
scenes.visual: The flashing subset turns grey. Label: activity-dependent tagging, then silencing.
scenes.narration: Then they tagged those neurons genetically, and silenced them.

scenes.tts: Predict. With the ensemble silenced, does the paw still pull away?
scenes.visual: The paw and filament again, with the greyed ensemble in an inset. Question: does the paw still pull away?
scenes.narration: Predict. With the ensemble silenced, does the paw still pull away?

scenes.tts: Yes. The withdrawal reflexes were preserved. But escape and avoidance fell.
scenes.visual: The paw lifts. Two bars beside it, escape and avoidance, drop. Label: reflex preserved; affective behaviour reduced.
scenes.narration: Yes. The withdrawal reflexes were preserved. But escape and avoidance fell.

scenes.tts: The reflex and the affective behaviour are two measurements, and they can come apart. This was male mice, in one model.
scenes.visual: Two separate gauges: reflex withdrawal, and affective-motivational behaviour. Scope tag: male mice, nerve-injury model, chosen behaviours; no verbal report.
scenes.narration: The reflex and the affective behaviour are two measurements, and they can come apart. This was male mice, in one model.

scenes.tts: In people, these cell-type manipulations cannot be done. So the human study here asks a different question: prediction.
scenes.visual: A human silhouette beside a brain scanner. Label: observational prediction study; cause untested.
scenes.narration: In people, these cell-type manipulations cannot be done. So the human study here asks a different question: prediction.

scenes.tts: Baliki and colleagues scanned adults whose back pain was still subacute. A year later, they asked who still had pain.
scenes.visual: Timeline: brain scan at baseline, arrow to one year, splitting into two groups, recovering and persisting. Label: Baliki and colleagues.
scenes.narration: Baliki and colleagues scanned adults whose back pain was still subacute. A year later, they asked who still had pain.

scenes.tts: Recovering meant a set drop in pain intensity. It did not mean pain-free.
scenes.visual: On screen: recovering = pain intensity fell past a 20 percent cutoff; 20 recovering, 19 persisting. Note: recovering did not mean pain-free.
scenes.narration: Recovering meant a set drop in pain intensity. It did not mean pain-free.

scenes.tts: Stronger baseline connectivity between medial prefrontal cortex and nucleus accumbens predicted who persisted.
scenes.visual: Brain outline with a line linking medial prefrontal cortex and nucleus accumbens. On screen: ROC area 0.83.
scenes.narration: Stronger baseline connectivity between medial prefrontal cortex and nucleus accumbens predicted who persisted.

scenes.tts: That area is a pair-ordering probability. It is not a cause, and not one person's risk.
scenes.visual: Two patient icons, one from each group, compared side by side; the persisting one has the higher score. Labels: pair-ordering; not a cause; not one person's risk.
scenes.narration: That area is a pair-ordering probability. It is not a cause, and not one person's risk.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: in rodent models, the wiring, the cord and the immune cells all change. In mice, affective behaviour can be separated from the reflex. In people, we have association and prediction.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: the three-level schematic fully lit (ganglion, dorsal horn with immune cells, brain), with the affective-behaviour dial drawn apart from the reflex arrow. Corner tag: rodents, mechanism; people, association and prediction.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: in rodent models, the wiring, the cord and the immune cells all change. In mice, affective behaviour can be separated from the reflex. In people, we have association and prediction.
